title: Promoted Listings and Seller Tools: Which Ones Actually Move Product

facts.fact: The guide advises starting ad rates at roughly half the platform's suggested rate on a batch of listings and watching for two weeks before stepping up.
facts.quote: A practical approach is to start at roughly half the suggested rate on a batch of listings and watch for two weeks.

facts.fact: The guide recommends sending watcher offers with a modest discount of five to ten percent and a short expiry.
facts.quote: send a modest discount, five to ten percent, with a short expiry.

facts.fact: The guide says many sellers find an acceptance-rate cliff for watcher offers somewhere around an 8 to 12 percent discount, where acceptance jumps.
facts.quote: Most sellers find a cliff, often somewhere around eight to twelve percent, where acceptance jumps.

facts.fact: The guide advises not sending offers on a listing until it has had about a week at full price.
facts.quote: Give a listing a week to find its audience at full price.

facts.fact: The guide's example policy runs new listings unpromoted for the first seven to ten days to observe organic performance.
facts.quote: New listings run unpromoted for the first seven to ten days so you can see organic performance.

facts.fact: In the guide's example policy, listings with fewer than twenty views by day ten get promoted at the seller's tested base rate.
facts.quote: Anything with fewer than twenty views by day ten gets promoted at your tested base rate.

facts.fact: In the guide's example policy, listings older than sixty days receive one round of aggressive treatment combining promotion, a price cut, and an offer sweep.
facts.quote: Anything past sixty days gets one round of aggressive treatment

facts.fact: The guide cites a listing up for ninety days with steady views and no sales as needing a lower price or better photos rather than a relist.
facts.quote: A listing that has been up for ninety days with steady views and no sales does not need a fresh start

facts.fact: The guide illustrates how ad fees compound by citing a four percent ad rate and a thirteen percent final value fee stacking on the same sale.
facts.quote: Four percent here and thirteen percent there feels small individually and collectively can turn a twenty percent margin into single digits.

facts.fact: The guide recommends a promotion holdout test run for one month, comparing a promoted group against an unpromoted group of comparable inventory.
facts.quote: Promote one group, leave the other alone, and run it for a month.

facts.fact: The guide recommends running the promotion holdout test once a quarter rather than continuously.
facts.quote: Run this test once a quarter rather than continuously.

facts.fact: The guide's worked example assumes promotion moves sell-through from 20 percent to 25 percent on a group of 100 items, yielding five extra sales.
facts.quote: If promotion moved your sell through from twenty percent to twenty five percent on a group of a hundred items, that is five extra sales.

facts.fact: The guide suggests batching sharing into two short daily blocks focused on the top thirty items by likes and the newest inventory.
facts.quote: Sharing is worth batching into two short daily blocks rather than spreading across the day.
